[*HUAWEI-vlan2] name voice

record.FuncDef:
The port command sets a default VLAN for interfaces and adds interfaces to the VLAN.
The undo port command deletes the interfaces from the default VLAN and restores the default VLAN ID.
By default, no default VLAN is set for interfaces.

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies an interface type.
-

Specifies the start number of an interface.
-

Specifies the end number of an interface.
-

Specifies the name of an interface.
-

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
Frames sent from user hosts are untagged and those sent from a remote device may also be untagged. However, a switching device only processes and forwards tagged frames. Therefore, tags need to be added to the untagged frames on the switching device. To implement this function, run the port default vlan command to configure a default VLAN on an interface of the switching device. After this function is enabled, the interface adds the default VLAN ID to received untagged frames.
After a default VLAN is configured on an interface: The interface inserts the default VLAN ID to a received untagged frame if the link type of the interface is access or hybrid.
When the interface receives a tagged frame:
If the interface type is access and the VLAN ID in the tag is the same as the default VLAN ID, the access interface forwards the frame.
If the VLAN ID in the tag is different from the default VLAN ID, the access interface discards the frame.
If the interface type is hybrid and the VLAN ID in the tag is in the permitted VLAN ID list, the hybrid interface forwards the frame.
If the VLAN ID is not in the permitted VLAN ID list, the hybrid interface discards the frame.
When the interface sends a tagged frame:
If the interface type is access, the access interface removes the VLAN tag and then forwards the frame.
If the interface type is hybrid, the hybrid interface removes or keeps the VLAN tag in a frame as required and then forwards the frame.
Prerequisites
The link type of the interface has been configured as access or hybrid or dot1q-tunnel using the port link-type command.
Precautions
The port command has the same function as the port default vlan command in the interface view.
Before you specify an interface range, note that:
1.The interface types must be the same.
2.The interfaces in the range must exist.
3.If the port command is run more than once, all configurations take effect.
4.The interface to be added to a VLAN must be a Layer 2 interface. If the interface is a Layer 3 interface, run the portswitch command to switch the interface to Layer 2. The port default vlan command cannot be configured on physical interfaces that are added to an Eth-Trunk.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
vlan | write

Examples (source text):
# Add GE interfaces 0/1/0 to 0/1/1 to VLAN 3.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] interface GigabitEthernet 1/0/0
[~HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/0] portswitch
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/0] port link-type access
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/0] quit
[*HUAWEI] interface GigabitEthernet 1/0/1
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] portswitch
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] port link-type access
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] quit
[*HUAWEI] vlan 3
[*HUAWEI-vlan3] port GigabitEthernet 1/0/0 to 1/0/1

record.FuncDef:
The port link-type command configures a link type on an Ethernet interface.
The undo port link-type command restores the default link type.
The default link type of an interface is hybrid.

ParaDef.Info:
Configures the link type of an interface as hybrid.
-

Configures the link type of an interface as trunk.
-

Configures the link type of an interface as dot1q-tunnel.
-

Configures the link type of an interface as access.
-

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
Different types of interfaces are applicable to different scenarios: An access interface connects to a user host and is usually used on an access link. The frames transmitted on the access link are untagged Ethernet frames. If an access interface is configured with a default VLAN, the interface adds a tag to the packet and sets the VID in the tag to the default VLAN ID. A trunk interface is used to connect to another device and is usually used on a trunk link. A trunk interface allows frames from multiple VLANs to pass through. A hybrid interface can connect to a user host or another device. A hybrid interface can connect to an access link or a trunk link. A hybrid interface allows frames from multiple VLANs to pass through. A Dot1q-tunnel interface is mainly used on carrier networks. It adds another 802.1Q tag to 802.1Q tagged packets to expand VLAN space. In this manner, packets from private VLANs can be transparently transmitted to the public network.
Precautions
The port link-type command cannot be configured on physical interfaces that are added to an Eth-Trunk.
A Layer 3 interface must be switched to a Layer 2 interface using the portswitch command. The link type of the Layer 2 interface is hybrid by default. You can run the port link-type command to modify its link type.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
vlan | write

Examples (source text):
# Configure the link type of GE 1/0/1 as trunk.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] portswitch
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] port link-type trunk

CLIs: port trunk allow-pass vlan { { { <vlan-id1> [ to <vlan-id2> ] } &<1-10> } | all }
undo port trunk allow-pass vlan { { { <vlan-id1> [ to <vlan-id2> ] } &<1-10> } | all }
record.FuncDef:
The port trunk allow-pass vlan command adds a trunk or a hybrid interface to a VLAN.
The undo port trunk allow-pass vlan command deletes a trunk or a hybrid interface from a VLAN.
By default, a trunk or hybrid interface is not added to a VLAN.

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies the start VLAN ID.
The value is an integer ranging from 1 to 4094.

Specifies the end ID of a VLAN.
The value is an integer ranging from 1 to 4094.

Specifies all VLANs.
-

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
A trunk interface can be added to multiple VLANs and is generally used to connect network devices. If frames with one or more VLAN tags need to pass through a trunk interface, run the port trunk allow-pass command to add the trunk interface to the VLAN(s). In this manner, the trunk interface forwards these frames without removing the VLAN tags.
Prerequisites
An interface has been configured as a trunk or a hybrid interface using the port link-type command.
Precautions
The trunk interface to be added to VLANs must be a Layer 2 interface. If the interface is a Layer 3 interface, run the portswitch command to change the interface to a Layer 2 interface. If you run the port trunk allow-pass command more than once on the same interface, all the configured VLANs take effect on the interface.
Running the undo port trunk allow-pass vlan command on an interface deletes the MAC address entries of the interface.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
vlan | write

Examples (source text):
# Add the trunk interface GE 1/0/1 to VLANs 2 to 10, 100, and 200.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] portswitch
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] port link-type trunk
[*HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] port trunk allow-pass vlan 2 to 10 100 200

record.FuncDef:
The portswitch command changes the mode of an Ethernet interface from Layer 3 to Layer 2.
The undo portswitch command changes the mode of an Ethernet interface from Layer 2 to Layer 3.
By default, an Ethernet interface works in Layer 3 mode.
record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
By default, Ethernet interfaces of Layer 3 devices such as the Router operate in Layer 3 mode. If these interfaces need to be added to a VLAN or other Layer 2 configurations need to be performed on these interfaces, the mode of these interfaces needs to be switched to Layer 2.
Precautions
When you run this command on an interface, the mode switching configuration takes effect when only attribute configurations (such as shutdown and description configurations) or configurations that are supported on Layer 2 or Layer 3 interfaces (such as mode lacp and lacp system-id configurations) exist on the interface. Configurations that are not supported by the interface mode after the switch should not exist.
If other interfaces are configured to borrow IP addresses of the Ethernet and GE interfaces, the corresponding Ethernet and GE interfaces do not support the portswitch command.
In addition, only Layer 2 Eth-Trunk interfaces can be bound to or unbound from a VLAN. If an Eth-Trunk interface is changed from the Layer 3 to Layer 2 mode, all Layer 3 functions and identifiers of the Eth-Trunk interface are disabled, and the system MAC address is used.
Eth-Trunk member interfaces do not support changes of the working mode between Layer 2 and Layer 3.
If an interface has sub-interfaces, interface mode switching affects forwarding of all the sub-interfaces. After an Ethernet interface is switched from Layer 3 mode to Layer 2 mode, the link type of the Ethernet interface is Hybrid by default, and no default VLAN is configured for the interface.
You can run this command to switch a FlexE interface between Layer 2 and Layer 3 only when the FlexE interface is configured to work in timeslot mode.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
vlan | write

Examples (source text):
# Switch the mode of GE 1/0/1 to Layer 2.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] interface GigabitEthernet 1/0/1
[~HUAWEI-GigabitEthernet1/0/1] portswitch
# Switch the mode of Eth-Trunk 1 to Layer 2.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] interface eth-trunk 1
[*HUAWEI-Eth-Trunk1] portswitch

record.FuncDef:
The vlan command creates a VLAN and displays the VLAN view. If the VLAN already exists, the VLAN view is displayed.
The undo vlan command deletes the VLAN.
By default, no VLAN exists.

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies a VLAN ID.
The value is an integer ranging from 1 to 4094.

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
To reduce broadcast domains and enhance security on a complex network, VLANs can be created on the network to isolate the devices that do not need to communicate with each other.
Precautions
The vlan command creates a VLAN and displays the VLAN view. If a VLAN has been created, the VLAN view is displayed after this command is used. If you run the vlan command more than once, all the created VLANs take effect. If a VLAN has been created, using this command does not create the same VLAN or modify the VLAN configuration. After a VLAN is created, both the vlan and vlan batch configurations exist in the configuration file.

Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
vlan | write

Examples (source text):
# Create VLAN 2. If it already exists, display the VLAN 2 view.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] vlan 2

record.FuncDef:
The vlan description command configures a description for a user VLAN.
The undo vlan description command deletes the description of a user VLAN.
By default, no description is configured for any user VLAN.

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies the VLAN ID in the inner VLAN tag carried in packets that a user-VLAN sub-interface receives.
The value is an integer ranging from 1 to 4094.

Specifies the VLAN ID in the outer VLAN tag carried in packets that a user-VLAN sub-interface receives.
The value is an integer ranging from 1 to 4094.

Specifies a description.
The value is a string of 1 to 128 case-sensitive characters, spaces supported.

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
When multiple user-VLAN sub-interfaces configured on the same interface can be accessed by different VLAN users, to help you learn user VLAN information, run the vlan description command to configure a description for the user VLAN.
Precautions
After the vlan description command is run, the system displays only the description of the VLAN with the same ID as the User-VLAN configured on the interface.
In VS mode, this command is supported only by the admin VS.

Default Level:
2: Configuration level

ethernet | write

commands.title: eq | lt | gt | neq | range (ACL port pool view)

record.PageTitle: eq | lt | gt | neq | range (ACL port pool view)
record.FuncDef:
The eq command adds a port number to an ACL port pool.
The lt command adds multiple port numbers to an ACL port pool, with the numbers of the ports to be added less than a specific value.
The gt command adds multiple port numbers to an ACL port pool, with the numbers of the ports to be added greater than a specific value.
The neq command removes a port number from an ACL port pool.
The range command adds multiple port numbers to an ACL port pool, with the numbers of the ports to be added ranging from the start port number to the end port number.
The undo { eq | lt | gt | neq | range } command deletes the port number range from a created ACL port pool.
By default, no port number exists in an ACL port pool.

ParaDef.Info:
Specify start port number.
The value is an integer ranging from 0 to 65535.

Specifies the end port.
The value is an integer ranging from 0 to 65535.

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
In typical ACL usage scenarios, such as in QoS policy scenarios, a user may need to match both the source and destination port numbers. To match an ACL rule against multiple source and destination port numbers to implement a QoS policy, the user needs to create an ACL port pool and run the eq, gt, lt, or range command to add desired port numbers to the ACL port pool, or run the neq command to rule out unneeded port numbers from the ACL port number. When these port numbers are cohesive, you can run the eq, gt, lt, or range command to add multiple port numbers to the ACL port pool.
Prerequisites
An ACL port pool has been created using the acl port-pool command.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
acl | write

Examples (source text):
# Set the port number range to 5-100 for an ACL port pool named p1.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] acl port-pool p1
[*HUAWEI-acl-port-pool-p1] range 5 100

record.FuncDef:
The mode command configures a timestamp-refresh instance mode.
The undo mode command deletes a timestamp-refresh instance mode.
By default, no timestamp-refresh instance mode is configured.

ParaDef.Info:
Indicates that the timestamp-refresh function takes effect in 2022-7 standard protocol mode.
-

Indicates that the timestamp-refresh function takes effect in common mode.
-

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
There are two modes for timestamp-refresh instances: common mode and 2022-7 mode. The purpose of creating a mode is to specify the method for the timestamp-refresh function to take effect. If the common mode is configured, the offset value automatically takes effect. If the 2022-7 mode is configured, the offset value needs to be delivered to make the timestamp-refresh function take effect.
Prerequisites
A timestamp-refresh instance has been configured using the multicast timestamp-refresh instance command.
Precautions
In VS mode, this command is supported only by the admin VS.
This command takes effect only for the XA chassis.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
forwarding | write

Examples (source text):
# Set a timestamp-refresh instance mode.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] multicast timestamp-refresh instance one
[*HUAWEI-mc-ts-rfsh-instance-one] mode 2022-7

commands.title: interface (BGP Flow Specification interface group view)

record.PageTitle: interface (BGP Flow Specification interface group view)
record.FuncDef:
The interface command adds an interface to a BGP Flow Specification interface group.
The undo interface command deletes an interface from a BGP Flow Specification interface group.
By default, no interfaces are added to a BGP Flow Specification interface group.
ParentView: BGP Flow Specification interface group view

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies the type of an interface.
-

Specifies the number of an interface.
The value is a string of 1 to 63 case-sensitive characters. It cannot contain spaces.

Specifies the name of an interface.
The value is a string of 1 to 63 case-sensitive characters. It cannot contain spaces.

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
Without a BGP Flow Specification interface group, the traffic filtering rules configured for BGP Flow Specification routes take effect globally, not on a specified interface. If a BGP Flow Specification interface group is configured, the traffic filtering rules configured for BGP Flow Specification routes also take effect on a specified interface. In this manner, traffic can be forwarded based on the rules of the BGP Flow Specification routes on the specified interface.
After a BGP Flow Specification interface group is created using the flow-interface-group command, you need to run the interface command to add an interface to the group.
Precautions
Sub-interfaces cannot be added to a BGP Flow Specification interface group. BGP Flow Specification interface groups support only the public address family. Therefore, interfaces configured with L2VPN, EVPN, and EVPL services cannot be added to a BGP Flow Specification interface group.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations
flow-route | write

Examples (source text):
# Add an interface to a BGP Flow Specification interface group.
<HUAWEI> system-view
[~HUAWEI] flow-interface-group 1

record.FuncDef:
The port command configures an interface number range for data backup.
The undo port command deletes the interface number range configured for data backup.
By default, no interface number range for data backup is configured for an IPsec instance.

ParaDef.Info:
Specifies a start interface number.

Specifies an end interface number. high-port-number must be greater than low-port-number, and the value difference must be 255.

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
In dual-system hot backup scenarios, to configure the interface number range for forwarding data backup in an IPsec instance, run the port command.
Precautions
After an IPsec instance is applied to an IPsec policy, the interface number range for data backup cannot be modified.
record.ExtraInfo:
Default Level:
2: Configuration level

Task Name and Operations:
Task Name | Operations

record.FuncDef:
The start command sets the start mode and end mode for an NQA test instance.
The undo start command stops the running NQA test instance. If the start at or start delay command is run but does not take effect, running the undo start command will delete the previous configuration. The undo start command functions the same as the stop command.
By default, the test stops automatically after test packets are sent.

ParaDef.Info:
Performs the test immediately.
-

End a test.
-

Start or end test at a time.
-

Start or end delay time.
-

The life time or delay time, in seconds.
The value is an integer ranging from 6 to 86399.

Set the test lifetime.
-

The date of test start or test end.
yyyy specifies the yea, which is an integer ranging from 1970 to 9999. mm specifies the month, which is an integer ranging from 1 to 12. dd
specifies the day, which is an integer ranging from 1 to 31.

Set the test start time, test end time, life time or delay time.
hh specifies the hour, which is an integer ranging from 0 to 23. mm specifies the minute, which is an integer ranging from 0 to 59. ss specifies the second, which is an integer ranging from 0 to 59.

Start test daily.
-

-

-

record.UsageGuidelines:
Usage Scenario
To set the start and end time for an NQA test instance, run the start command.
The main application scenarios of the command are as follows:
To start and stop a test instance at the specified time, run the start at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> end at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> command. To start a test instance at the specified time and stop it when a specified duration (in seconds) elapses, run the start at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> end lifetime seconds <second> command. To start a test instance after a specified delay (in seconds) and stop it at the specified time, run the start delay seconds <second> end at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> command. To start a test instance immediately and stop it when a specified duration (in seconds) elapses, run the start now end lifetime seconds <second> command. To start and stop a test instance at specified time every day, run the start daily <hh:mm:ss> to <hh:mm:ss> command.
Set a proper start mode for a test instance as needed.
Currently, generalflow test instances support the start now command only.
Configuration Impact
If the start daily command is run more than once, the latest configuration overrides the previous one.
Precautions
If the number of running test instances reaches the maximum number allowed by the system, the start command fails. For the same test instance, the start now command can be run again only after the previous test is complete.
When two NQA generalflow test instances that are bound to the same physical interface but different VLANs are performed at the same time, the test result may be inaccurate.
In non-periodic test scenarios, if a large number of test instances are concurrently executed, you need to wait for a period of time before starting new test instances.
When a test instance is scheduled to run at a specified time every day, if the system time is changed to fall within the configured start-end time window, test packets are sent.
If the parameters start at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> and end at <yyyy/mm/dd> <hh:mm:ss> are specified, the test duration is the period between start time and end time. The end at parameter does not mean the time when the test instance execution ends.
